title: DVB Common Interface / CI+ host (EN 50221 on an 8-bit PC Card bus): CAM power, CIS / COR, command interface messages over AXI4, TS routing
features: Card pins: ci_vcc_en, ci_reset, ci_cd_n, ci_a[14:0], ci_d_o / ci_d_oe / ci_d_i, CE#, REG#, OE#, WE#, IORD#, IOWR#, WAIT#, IREQ# (READY before I/O mode).
Power-up (CMD.power_on): VCC on, RESET high for RST_CLKS clocks, then READY awaited (STATUS.ready, READY interrupt); power-off by command, card removal or ENABLE off.
Bus cycles with programmable SETUP, STROBE and HOLD clocks, stretched by WAIT#; WAIT_MAX ends a stuck cycle (reads 0xFF, BUS_TO, TO_CNT).
CMD.cis_read copies CIS_LEN bytes of attribute memory (even addresses) to memory at CIS_ADDR; CMD.cor_write writes COR_VAL to COR_ADDR and enters I/O mode.

EN 50221 command interface: interface reset (RS, wait for FR); host-to-module messages of TX_LEN bytes from TX_ADDR (FR / HC handshake, size, data; FR_MAX polls before giving up); module-to-host messages polled (DA), sized (SR) and stored at RX_ADDR (up to RX_MAX bytes, RX_LEN, STATUS.rx_ovf), the buffer held until CMD.rx_arm.
Transport stream routed through the CAM (ci_mo_* out, ci_mi_* back, TS_CNT packets) with CTRL.ts_route in I/O mode, bypassed otherwise.
One AXI4 DMA engine: write bursts for CIS and RX data, read bursts for TX data (bytes packed 4 per word, little-endian).

fields.desc: controller on; 0 powers the card off
route the transport stream through the CAM (in I/O mode)
poll the command interface for module-to-host messages
strobe low at least STROBE + 1 (>= 3 for cards that use WAIT#)
strobe end to CE# high: HOLD + 1
longest WAIT# before the cycle is ended (0: no limit)
STATUS polls without FR before a TX or interface reset gives up (0: no limit)
power the card up (card present, ENABLE)
write the COR, enter I/O mode
free the RX buffer for the next message
the card is powered and ready
the RX buffer holds a message
the last message was longer than RX_MAX
the last TX gave up (FR_MAX) or lost the card
an AXI error response since power-up

regs.name: RX_LEN
regs.desc: Size of the last message received

fields.desc: TS packets returned by the CAM

irqs.name: READY
irqs.desc: the card is ready after power-up

irqs.name: CFG
irqs.desc: a CIS read, COR write or interface reset ended

irqs.name: RX
irqs.desc: a module-to-host message is in the RX buffer

irqs.name: IREQ
irqs.desc: the CAM requested an interrupt (I/O mode)

irqs.name: BUS_TO
irqs.desc: a bus cycle was ended by WAIT_MAX

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: an AXI error response in a CIS write, TX read or RX write (with CFG, TX_DONE or RX)

sequence: Write TIMING, WAITS, POLL, CIS_ADDR, CIS_LEN, COR, TX / RX buffer registers and IRQ_ENABLE, then CTRL.enable.
On DET with STATUS.present write CMD.power_on; on READY write CMD.cis_read and parse the CIS in memory on CFG (it gives the COR address and value).
Write COR and CMD.cor_write (CFG), CMD.if_reset (CFG), then CTRL.poll and CTRL.ts_route.
Send a message: fill the TX buffer, write TX_LEN and CMD.tx_start; TX_DONE ends it (check STATUS.tx_fail).
On RX read RX_LEN bytes from the RX buffer, then write CMD.rx_arm.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
One DMA job at a time on one engine: CIS and RX data use the write channel, TX data the read channel.
The card bus runs on the core clock; the I/O mode command interface sits at I/O addresses 0..3. ci_d_oe enables the host's data drivers.
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
